text:
Amanda Li: Heads up — I opened a quick proposal for trace TTL defaults by environment. TL;DR: prod hot 90d / cold 365d, staging hot 30d / cold 90d, dev hot 7d (cold off).
Raj Patel: Nice. What did you mean by hot vs cold here? indexes + fast query vs S3 raw?
Amanda Li: Exactly. Hot = trace index + materialized summary shards (fast search, flamegraph), Cold = object store + minimal index for retrieval.
Taylor Nguyen: Are we sure 90d hot for prod is necessary? Costs spike with high-sampling services.
Zoe Kim: If we reduce hot ttl we lose quick debugging history for long-running incidents. We should make this SLA-driven: customers with enterprise contracts get longer hot TTLs.
Mike O'Connor: +1 to SLA overrides. Also consider per-service overrides for analytics pipelines vs user-facing endpoints.
Raj Patel: Implementation question: do we set TTL at ingest time on spans, or run periodic compaction to move to cold?
Amanda Li: Plan is ingest tag + collector writes metadata to ClickHouse then lifecycle worker moves blobs to S3 and updates index pointers. That lets search route to cold transparently.
Taylor Nguyen: Sounds reasonable. Concern: tracing queries that touch cold become slow and can blow up dashboards. Need explicit UI affordance ("Include cold results") and default to hot-only for dashboards.
Zoe Kim: Yep. Console UX: add a dropdown on trace search (hot only / include cold / cold-only) and warn about latency/cost.
infra-bot: lifecycle-worker job started for bucket trace-shard-2026-03-17 (job id 4421) :gear:
Mike O'Connor: Also, sampling interacts with TTL. For high-volume services we recommend aggressive sampling + longer cold TTL for samples that matter.
Raj Patel: How do we handle traces that are rehydrated to hot (rehydration on-demand)? We need quota protections.
Amanda Li: Proposal: rehydrate via async job with rate-limited queue per org and a budget token charge (visible in billing). Rehydrate keeps trace hot for a configurable short window (e.g. 24h).
Taylor Nguyen: Can we avoid rehydration by keeping a small summarized index for cold traces (span counts, tags, duration hist)? Then many queries won't need full rehydration.
Zoe Kim: Good idea — store a compact trace metadata row (trace_id, service list, span_count, duration, error_flag, key_tags). That makes most searches fast.
Raj Patel: For exporters: we should ensure OTLP/gRPC exporters also attach environment label and sampling_decision for downstream TTL routing. Otherwise worker can't decide TTL.
Amanda Li: Yep, require `redwood.env` and `trace.ttl_hint` optional tag. Collector should map `trace.ttl_hint` to lifecycle tier if present.
Mike O'Connor: Edge-case: internal infra spans from agents (k8s probes) are noisy. We should default to drop or very short TTL unless explicit opt-in.
Taylor Nguyen: Ops asked about rollback semantics. If we change default TTL via rollout, older traces keep their original metadata. We must document that changing default doesn't retroactively move existing data.
Zoe Kim: Agreed — add a Console banner when TTL defaults change and a migration job option for admins to backfill.
Amanda Li: Next steps: I'll open RFC with config snippet and api shape. Example snippet: ```yaml
trace_ttl_defaults:
  prod:
    hot_days: 90
    cold_days: 365
  staging:
    hot_days: 30
    cold_days: 90
  dev:
    hot_days: 7
    cold_days: 0
```
Raj Patel: Can you add the SLA override API and rehydrate flow? I'll review.
Amanda Li: Will do. Anyone opposed to default numbers? :thinking_face:
Taylor Nguyen: Fine from me, but put a knob for perc-based sampling per service so users can trade cost vs retention.
Zoe Kim: +1. Also add console telemetry to show hot vs cold query latency and cost impact per org.
Mike O'Connor: Sounds good. I can pick up lifecycle worker PR once RFC lands.
Amanda Li: Great — thanks all. I'll drop the RFC link here when it's up.
Amanda Li: RFC: https://redwood-internal/rfcs/trace-ttl-policy (draft) :memo:
